skyline.about: The 360-degree sunset skyline behind the fight (src/fight/skyline.ts): a 10:1 strip (src/assets/skyline/, baked by scripts/skyline-bake.mjs with its two ends cross-faded over seamOverlapPx so the wrap has no seam) on a cylinder of `radius` m and `heightMetres` m that follows the camera, its horizon (`horizonFraction` down the strip) at the camera's eye level, unlit, unfogged, drawn first with no depth write; the sand floor, its colour, grid and fog are untouched and draw over it. The flat `sky` colour shows until the strip lands (fetched after the first frame, `loadAfterFirstFrameMs` later), then it fades in over `fadeSeconds`. `brightness` multiplies the strip (1 = as painted) so the hero and boss stay readable; `yawDegrees` turns the strip about the vertical. ?sky=v1 (`query` = `v1`) draws today's flat sky and fetches nothing. 8192 wide WebP q82: Dom's quality-first pick, see the PR's size table. YAW FOLLOW (Dom 2026-10-27: the alien was rarely seen): the strip turns by `yawDegrees` + `yawFollow` x the camera's yaw (0 = fixed in world yaw, 1 = glued to the view), eased over `yawFollowSeconds` so it drifts after a turn like a far backdrop; `followOffsetDegrees` -90 (the follow only) puts the alien dead ahead at the page's first heading (about 8 degrees). `face` is the alien face centre in the picture (fraction across, down; the test reads it to keep the face in the clear sky band above the HUD at 375 wide). ?skyfollow=v1 (`followQuery`, `followV1`) = fixed in world yaw at `yawDegrees` (0), as before.

plate.about: The skyline as a far backdrop PLATE (src/fight/skyplate.ts; Dom 2026-10-27, portrait phone: the 360-degree strip showed a tenth of a 10:1 picture blown up to a pink blur and the alien face could never fit). The plate is a `spanDegrees` arc of the strip's far cylinder (`radius`), facing the camp (it follows the camera's heading with the strip's follow rows, ?skyfollow=v1 pins it there): the face is dead ahead of the page's first heading (about -Z), turned by `turnDegrees` more (derived from `face`, so a new picture needs no yaw row), showing the picture `file` (src/assets/skyline/) at its NATIVE aspect, never stretched: a window of the picture `cropAspect` wide to tall is cut around `face` (u, v: the alien face centre as a fraction across and down the picture; the whole picture when it is no wider than that), and the arc is as tall as that window needs at its width. `horizonFraction` is the picture's horizon row, a fraction down it. `faceElevationDegrees` puts the face that many degrees above the eye's level (so the pitched-up phone camera has it in view; the picture's own horizon then sits below the eye, where the cloud sea meets the melted sand). The edges fade to nothing (`edgeFadeFraction` each side, `topFadeFraction`, `bottomFadeFraction`, fractions of the plate) into a plain sky gradient (`sky`: `hazeColor` at the bottom, `horizonColor` at the picture's horizon row, `topColor` at the top, a cylinder `halfHeightMetres` either side of the eye, `rings` rows) that is the sky everywhere else. THE PICTURE (Dom's Smiling Cosmic Titan Over Cloudsea, 2508x627 = exactly 4:1, shown whole at native proportions, WebP q88, 121 KB; horizon 80% down, face centre at 58.5% across and 63% down, moon and face in the middle half, edges fade to the sky colour, the top 40% plain blue): swapping the picture again is `file`, `cropAspect`, `horizonFraction` and `face`; nothing else changes (a picture wider than `cropAspect` is cut to that window around `face`, a narrower one is shown whole). The arc draws at SKYLINE_ORDER + `orderOffset`, over the folded cloud floor (fold.orderOffset) and under the sand, so inside its span the picture's own cloud sea shows and the floor's clouds carry on either side and below it; the plain sky gradient draws first of all. The old 360-degree strip's picture (`skyline.file`, 7782x820) stays for the rollback: ?skyplate=v1. ?skyplate=v1 (`query` = `v1`) draws the old whole 360-degree strip. ?sky=v1, ?skyfollow=v1 and ?skyfold=v1 keep their meaning.

anim.about: SMALL CODED MOTION on the plate (src/fight/skyanim.ts; Dom 2026-10-27 'small motion on the static image', lean: no video, 0 extra bytes today). Presentation only: the plate material gets a few shader lines and uniforms (clock, shifts, band), so a frame costs one clock tick and a few uniform writes. Positions are fractions across (u) and down (v, y down) the PLATE picture, radii are fractions of the picture's WIDTH (the circle stays round whatever the aspect). `on`/`query`/`off`: ?skyanim=off turns it all off (the plain plate); `respectReducedMotion` true = prefers-reduced-motion also turns it off; the clock stops while the tab is hidden. `light` is the sun direction (x right, y up, z toward the viewer), used only when a designer surface map is lit. GLOBE (the small world in the titan's raised hand): `centre`, `radius`; `secondsPerTurn` is one full turn of the fake spin (the sphere's own pixels re-mapped under a circle mask, longitude shifted and mirror-folded so it never seams), `swingDegrees` 0 = a continuous turn, above 0 = a swing of that many degrees each way instead; `highlight` is a soft moving glint (`strength`, `size` and `orbit` in disc radii, `lift` raises its path, `orbitSeconds` per lap). PLANET (the red-pink planet): `centre`, `radius`, `secondsPerTurn` with `swingDegrees` (a slow swing, since its terminator is baked into the picture), `lowerFadeFrom` (disc-radius y below which the swing fades out, where the cloud sea crosses the disc), `glow` (rim glow `color`, `strength`, `pulseSeconds`). GLISTEN (a soft additive sweep over the ring technology): a mask derived in the shader from bright (`lumaFrom`) high-contrast (`edgeLo`..`edgeHi`) edge pixels that are cool-toned (blue above red by `coolFrom`, so the lilac stone and cyan glow glisten and the warm face does not) inside `box` (u0,u1,v0,v1); a band `width` wide (fraction), tilted by `slant`, `color`, `strength`, sweeps the box in `sweepSeconds` every `periodSeconds`. DESIGNER LAYERS (docs/SKY-LAYERS.md): each `file` is '' (made from the flattened plate, today) or a .webp in src/assets/skyline/: globe.file = an equirectangular surface map (2:1, 256x128 or 512x256, sRGB, alpha ok) that then spins for real and is lit by `light` (`mapLit` 0..1); planet.file = the same for the planet (1024x512, with alpha); glisten.file = a greyscale mask (red channel = where it glistens; the plate's size or smaller, 1254x314 is plenty). plate.file swaps in the clean plate (no globe or planet baked in) at the same row shape. A new layer is one row change; the shader, rows and tests stay.

views.about: How much of the strip shows (src/fight/skyview.ts). Dom picked B (2026-10-27): `default` names the variant the page draws with no link; ?skyview=a|b|c picks one; ?skyview=v1 (`v1`) is the look before this (no melt, no lowering, nothing here runs); ?sky=v1 is still the flat sky. The camera, zoom and fight framing are never touched. Per variant: fogColor ('' = the scene's) is the strip's horizon haze (its lower band at horizonFraction, as drawn at `brightness`) and fogDensity (0 = the scene's, exp-squared) fogs the far sand into it; fadeStartDegrees / fadeEndDegrees (0/0 = off) melt the sand and its grid to transparent by how far below the horizon the camera sees it (solid at start and steeper, gone at end and shallower; an angle so it follows the strip's lowered bottom edge at any camera height, the phone fight camera looks 32 degrees down so its top edge is 8.6 degrees under the horizon), so the strip behind shows; dropMetres lowers the whole strip (the horizon of the image sits that far below the eye), heightMetres (0 = the row's) resizes it; brightness replaces the strip's own so the HUD reads over its bright cloud band. foeFade (true/false) fades the opponents and their gear by the same band measured at their feet, so a far boss dissolves into the clouds where the sand under him does (src/fight/foefade.ts; the hero is never faded; needs a band); ?foefade=v1 (foeFadeQuery / foeFadeV1) turns it off. A = fog only; B = fade + lowered strip + haze fog; C = lowered strip only.

fold.about: The folded floor (src/fight/skyfold.ts, Dom 2026-10-27: fold the image so the lower part becomes the floor). The strip's lower cloud band is laid flat on the ground under the sand: its horizon row (variant bandTopFraction, a fraction of the image height down from the top) is the far edge at farMetres, its bottom edge (bandBottomFraction) the near edge at nearMetres, the picture's x following the cylinder's yaw so the clouds under the horizon line up with the sky above. Rows are spaced the way a flat floor is seen (equal steps in 1/distance), so the clouds shrink toward the horizon. It follows the camera, sits at groundY, is unlit and unfogged, draws at SKYLINE_ORDER + orderOffset (after the strip, before the sand) with no depth write, and fades in with the strip; the far featherFraction of it fades to nothing so it melts into the sky behind. Only built when the sand melts (?skyview is not v1) and the strip is on. ?skyfold=v1 (`v1`) builds nothing; ?skyfold=a|b picks a variant, `default` is the no-link one (B: A's rows pulled across the ground are streaky spikes, B is the same band softened). A reuses the strip's own texture (file empty, no download); B loads `file` (src/assets/skyline/, baked by scripts/skyfold-bake.mjs: the band softened and tileable) after the first frame. around / rings are the mesh's segment counts.

duel.about: The arena theme V1's scene (src/fight/scene.ts) lights the duel with, in place of an arena-themes.json row: V2's sky, hemisphere and sun, the sun pushed out along V2's direction to clear V1's shadow frustum (near 1, far 70). V1's own exposure-dependent effects read `exposure`; `floor` names the arena-defs.json floor row the foot dust uses.
